channel.title: Frisco ISD Bond Facts
channel.description: Updates on the Frisco ISD 2027 bond, District spending, trustee votes and public records, using the District's own numbers.

item.title: 2018 bond, line by line: new buildings ran about $60 million over, maintenance $27 million under
item.description: The District's quarterly capital plan shows the arts center, Wilkinson, Panther Creek, Wortham and other new facilities about $60 million over budget, general maintenance funded at $82.9 million against $110 million promised, and $47.2 million of projects on hold.

item.title: Frisco ISD still owes $149 million in interest on $21 million of old capital appreciation bonds
item.description: State Bond Review Board data show $169.6 million in CAB payments still owed as of August 31, 2025. None of Frisco ISD's eight closest peers has any CABs.

item.title: District announces the $412.6 million recommendation, with no tax rate projection
item.description: Frisco ISD says 91% of the 83 committee members present approved the three year package. The committee votes again January 19, 2027, after a community survey, and the Board receives it in February. The announcement does not mention tax rates; the District's own model shows a 29.92 cent peak in FY2033.

item.title: Opinion: A bond plan I could support
item.description: Stephen Jordan's five conditions for a bond: wait for the 2027 Legislature, earn back voter trust, cap it at about $400 million with no rate increase even if growth slows, no bonds for short life items, and a project list for every school before the board votes.

item.title: The committee's $412.6 million package keeps raising the rate after FY2031
item.description: The committee's slide stops at FY2031 (27.42 cents). The District's own model shows the debt tax rate peaking at 29.92 cents in FY2033, about $144 a year on the median home, and 33.04 cents if the tax base stops growing.

item.title: Bond committee recommends a three year, $412.6 million package
item.description: On November 17 the 2027 Bond Planning Committee recommended $412.6 million, down from a $1.03 billion project list. It includes $97.6 million for technology, buses and equipment.

item.title: Lone Star Furnishings payments since Dr. Fouche became superintendent
item.description: The District paid Lone Star $15,517 from April through August 6, 2026, after Dr. Fouche became superintendent and before his disclosure was posted.

item.title: Lone Star Furnishings has backed school bond campaigns across North Texas
item.description: Texas Ethics Commission records show 10 contributions totaling $21,500 from Lone Star Furnishings to school bond PACs, including $5,000 to Vote for Frisco ISD in October 2024.

item.title: What Frisco's A rating looks like with achievement taken out
item.description: Frisco ISD earned a 91. With the income-linked Student Achievement scores removed, Texas Trustee Data calculates an 85, about the same drop as other affluent districts.

item.title: Every trustee vote, tracked
item.description: A running record of how each Frisco ISD trustee voted on every recorded item since September 2026, with split votes highlighted.

item.title: November 16 board meeting: Staley, cash on hand, October purchases
item.description: The Staley demolition resolution, $418.5 million on hand at September 30, October purchases over $100,000 including $450,000 for marketing, and the 2026 tax roll.

item.title: District asks the Attorney General to withhold its college outcome reports
item.description: Frisco ISD asked for a new ruling on its National Student Clearinghouse StudentTracker reports. Other districts, including Dallas ISD, publish theirs.

item.title: 3 of 7 trustees have replied on Lone Star Furnishings
item.description: Trustees Manduva, Wamhoff and Maddox responded. Trustees Davis, Elad, Salas and Sample have not.

item.title: District says it will not bring a $1 billion bond to voters
item.description: The test is the final number. Today's 27 cent rate supports about $400 million, by the District's own estimate.

item.title: District model shows the debt tax rate peaking at 36 cents
item.description: The committee's Bond Planning Model shows the full package peaking at 36.06 cents in FY2033, about $447 a year more on the median home.
